messages:
maria: quick check - i'm finishing a docs PR for the audit-exports page and noticed multiple retention field names across examples plus a terraform snippet that still shows raw prompt text. SOC2 reviewers will flag raw prompts.

kevin: can you list what names are in use today? i can grep the repo.

maria: saw `expires_at` (ISO string) in JS, `ttl_seconds` in python, and `retention_days` in terraform/examples. also one terraform block had `prompt_text: '...secret...'`. bad teaching moment.

anya: suggestion: pick `retention_period_days` (int) as canonical for SDK and infra examples, and add a structured shape example for the API: `retention_policy: {type: 'days', value: 365}`. that maps nicely to UI controls.

security: +1. remove any example showing full prompt content. instead show `prompt_id: "p_<hash>"` and include a short paragraph: "Retrieval of raw prompts requires an audited admin KMS unwrap and manual approval." include link to internal export playbook.

compliance: SOC2 wording: always use "retained for N days" and append "may be retained longer for legal hold or investigations." avoid words like "permanent". also add a short FAQ entry: "How do we handle legal hold?" that references the manual approval process.

maria: plan: 1) update JS/Py/Go/Ruby/Terraform snippets to `retention_period_days`, 2) replace raw prompt examples with `prompt_id` pseudonymization and short KMS unwrap note, 3) add migration mapping table (expires_at/ttl_seconds -> retention_period_days), 4) add a tiny docs-lint rule to grep for `prompt_text`/`prompt:`.

kevin: i'll add the migration table and the CI grep. for the API ref i'll include the structured `retention_policy` example and a one-line migration snippet showing how to convert ISO `expires_at` to days (watch for timezone edge cases).

doc-bot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5543 by maria - "docs(security): harmonize retention fields; pseudonymize prompt examples; add migration mapping"

anya: can we also add a tiny example showing an admin lookup flow (high level) and mention that admin unwraps are recorded in audit logs with KMS event IDs? security, is that ok to mention?

security: ok to mention at a high level. add this sentence: "Admin retrievals are audit-logged and include KMS unwrap event IDs; retrievals require manual approval and are subject to compliance review." don't include internal URLs or screenshots in the public doc.

kevin: added a unit in docs tests that validates sample snippets against the canonical audit schema to catch drift. also added the grep-based lint to fail on `prompt_text` occurrences.

maria: perfect. i'll tag @security and @compliance on the PR for wording sign-off. after merge, squash and CHANGELOG entry: "docs(security): unify retention snippet names; remove raw prompt examples; document KMS-backed prompt lookup"

compliance: will review wording tomorrow morning. thanks for catching this.

maria: small but important cleanup for SOC2 readiness. thanks everyone.
